newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift but second-tier oils strong.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift but second-tier oils strong.

text.p: Leading Russian shares drifted down on Thursday afternoon, but dealers said second-tier oil companies were performing strongly and would rise more next week.

The Russian Trading System index had ticked down to 503.85 at 1100 GMT from 503.97 at the previous close. National power company UES eased to $0.4534 at 1325 GMT from $0.4660 and oil producer LUKoil dropped to $22.70 from $23.00.

"There is enough money to support the market," said CentreInvest trader Dmitry Nikitin, who saw the market steady through the end of the week. "Big institutional investors have invested and keep investing."
The RTS index has moved up from about 360 a month ago.
But leading liquid shares, which have seen the most growth recently as new funds pour into the market, could take a back seat to undervalued second-tier shares as investors look for new bargains.
"New people who really focused on blue chips did not have time to look at second tiers," said Alfa Capital's Alexander Bubnovsky.
Second-tier oil companies were lead performers on Thursday, with Purneftegaz prefs rising to $3.32 from $3.03 and Noyabrskneftegaz rising to $11.55 from $11.30.
Bubnovsky said investors were lined up to buy if a correction began, which lessened the chances for a price fall.
He predicted the market drifting before the weekend but said second tiers would fuel modest gains next week.
